exposure: Critical pulmonary stenosis (CPS) vs. non-CPS groups
Serum N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels
outcome: Efficacy of serum NT-proBNP levels in predicting critical pulmonary stenosis (CPS) in neonates
Correlation between Ln(NT-proBNP) levels and the transvalvular pulmonary gradient
Correlation between Ln(NT-proBNP) levels and pulmonary artery velocity
Predictive value of NT-proBNP for identifying neonatal CPS
Correlation between Ln(NT-proBNP) and length of hospital stay
cohort: 96 infants diagnosed with pulmonary stenosis (PS) by echocardiography, with 46 enrolled in the study (21 in the non-CPS group and 25 in the CPS group).
finding: Serum NT-proBNP level was positively correlated with PS severity and could be used as a biomarker to identify CPS in neonates.
